result.title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
result.comment: Equal contribution: Haofu Yang and Hongyang Yin. Corresponding authors: Ran Bi and Faguo Wu
result.summary: Parallel LLM agents tackle complex tasks by exploring multiple trajectories, yet useful discoveries remain isolated in individual execution histories. Existing sharing methods often select or summarize information before other agents' needs become clear, potentially overlooking details that become important later. We propose Ask on Demand (AOD), a communication framework that enables agents to seek targeted peer assistance when specific information needs arise. Upon an approved request, AOD retrieves relevant evidence from peer execution histories, selects a suitable peer, and generates a response tailored to the request. To determine when such assistance is worthwhile, we train a lightweight gate using paired team continuations, with supervision derived from final team outcomes and inference cost. Experiments on AppWorld and WebShop demonstrate that AOD consistently improves task performance over independent parallel execution while achieving lower inference cost than existing information-sharing baselines. These findings highlight the benefits of aligning peer communication with agents' evolving information needs to achieve more effective and efficient collaboration.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Ask on Demand 框架，让并行 LLM agent 在出现具体信息需求时向同伴发起定向请求，从对等执行历史中检索证据并生成定制回复；同时用配对团队延续结果与推理成本训练轻量门控，在 AppWorld 和 WebShop 上验证性能与成本收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“何时值得请求外部信息”的门控与证据检索，可能为 LVR 中的 LOOK/STOP 决策及成本感知的证据筛选提供方法线索，但该工作面向文本多 agent 通信，视觉状态迁移仍需核查。
